answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can treat every agent as a vertex in a trust graph, where edges form only after verifiable work or bonded stake. New identities start isolated, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents gains no edges and no reputation. Like a reef built coral by coral, trust accrues slowly through attested interactions, while creating a fake vertex costs real stake that is slashed on fraud. The violet line is simple: identity is cheap, but a trusted position in the graph is expensive to fake.
